title: Symmetries and Singularities
abstract: arXiv:2609.14663v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep neural networks are highly over-parameterized, and different parameter values represent the same predictive function. This makes their effective complexity difficult to measure using only the number of parameters or the rank of the Hessian. Singular Learning Theory addresses this issue through the local learning coefficient (LLC), which characterizes the effective complexity of a model near a given solution. Existing methods for estimating the LLC often rely on posterior sampling, which can be computationally expensive for large neural networks. This makes accurate LLC estimation difficult at scale. In this work, we use known structures in the model to simplify the analysis and make LLC estimation more tractable. Specifically, we study the LLC of a graph attention model by exploiting symmetries in both the graph structure and the attention parameters. translated_abstract: 深度神经网络高度过参数化，不同的参数值可以表示相同的预测函数。这使得仅通过参数数量或Hessian矩阵的秩来衡量模型的有效复杂性变得困难。奇异学习理论通过局部学习系数（LLC）来解决这一问题，该系数刻画了模型在给定解附近的有效复杂性。现有的LLC估计方法通常依赖于后验采样，这对于大型神经网络来说计算代价高昂，使得大规模下的准确LLC估计变得困难。在这项工作中，我们利用模型中已知的结构来简化分析，使LLC估计更加可行。具体而言，我们通过利用图结构和注意力参数中的对称性，研究了图注意力模型的LLC。我们通过师生设置建立了解析框架，并给出了显式的LLC估计
tldr: 本文通过利用图结构和注意力参数中的对称性，在师生设置下建立解析框架并给出显式的局部学习系数（LLC）估计，从而使图注意力模型的有效复杂性估计更加可行。
en_tdlr: This work exploits symmetries in graph structure and attention parameters to establish an analytic teacher-student framework with explicit local learning coefficient (LLC) estimates, making effective complexity estimation tractable for graph attention models.
